Comment accuracy at `fleet/run-engine.mjs` `suiteLine` (patch hunk @@ -404,7 +413,10 @@): the new comment asserts "A red suite's output arrives here already narrowed to the failing block". That invariant does not hold at the only live call site. `suiteLine` is called exactly once in the engine (`suiteLine(lastSuite, testCmd)` in the completeness-critic brief), and `lastSuite` is only ever assigned from `merge.suite`, which the two MERGED returns build as `{ passed: true, output: tail(suite.stdout + suite.stderr) }` — so `lastSuite.passed` is never `false` and the red branch is reached only by the unit pins in `test_run_engine_critic_inputs.mjs` and the new exam's leg (e). Nothing narrows an output on its way into this function; the branch simply must not re-cut whatever it is handed. The behaviour is correct and leg (e) [M5] pins it; only the stated reason is wrong, and in a file whose comments are load-bearing that is worth correcting. Suggested reword: "The red branch is a unit pin — the engine only ever adopts a green tree, so `lastSuite` is never red here (see the note above `suiteLine`). It carries the output whole rather than re-tailing it: whatever a caller hands in was already cut to the failing block, and a second cut would drop the very lines the block was chosen to keep."; M2 as literally worded is not satisfiable by any correct implementation: it asks that "the line of the completeness critic's brief beginning `Baseline: the suite is RED on BASE — `" contain the leg-naming line, but the excerpt that follows that prefix is a multi-line block, so the leg-naming line is a *later* physical line of the brief, never part of the prefix line itself.
